request:
Use wp-site-expert and other owning WordPress skills as appropriate. For each independent hypothetical request, give the route you actually load, concrete next decisions, required proof and limits. Decision-only: do not mutate sites, accounts or designs. No source images or live product runtime have been supplied.
1. Implement an approved Figma homepage exactly as editable WordPress content; someone suggests taste rules should replace its centered hero.
2. Approve a site from screenshots at 375 and 1440 pixels only.
3. Build plugin-owned onboarding/settings and a customer results surface without a design target.
4. Implement an approved screenshot as plugin-owned customer results and matching admin configuration.
5. Implement a linked selected Figma node exactly; structured design tools are available.
6. Add an interactive filter block preserving state through region navigation.
7. Approve a multistep signup from an automated accessibility scan of its first screen.
8. Turn a plugin dashboard into personalized AI recommendations and automatic actions.
9. Use a WebGL product story with non-linear scrolling on a WordPress site.
10. Build a new site inspired by a supplied screenshot.
11. Improve an existing page shown in a screenshot.
12. Generate the replacement design first for a growth-led landing page redesign.
13. Deliver an exact responsive system from only a cropped compressed desktop screenshot.
14. Add a pricing page to an existing screenshot-defined language.
15. Support English/Arabic and light/dark/system modes.
16. Migrate WordPress controls to newer ui/theme packages because TypeScript compiles.
17. Build custom modal, combobox and tabs for a plugin.
18. A consequential settings form faces duplicate submission, two-tab editing, slow responses and partial saves.
19. Approve browser and assistive-technology compatibility from one Chromium screenshot.
20. Approve a redesign where Figma, theme.json and CSS token values differ but each screenshot looks fine. A customer metric and screenshot also lack source evidence.
21. Extend an existing Tailwind WordPress panel; its developer suggests replacing the approved design with a Tailwind template and relying on dev-server CSS.
22. Make an editorial site premium with fashionable fonts, arbitrary fixed sizes and frontend-only typography.
23. Card insets match tokens but text is vertically misaligned; keep shrinking child padding.
24. Make all spacing identical multiples of eight to make a pricing section enterprise-grade.
25. A polished near-match has no independent source/candidate comparison; approve its spatial fidelity.
26. A 2880-pixel screenshot is supplied with unknown CSS viewport, DPR and export scale. Infer exact CSS values.
27. A fallback font changes hero wrapping. Fix its spacing before fonts load.
28. Frontend containers match theme.json but saved user Global Styles cause editor divergence. Which layer should be repaired?
29. Attractive cards have different borders and crops from the approved reference. Average visual craft and fidelity into one pass.
30. A one-page theme already has working presets; add a large token framework before correcting one gap.
31. Rename a launched semantic token without inspecting its consumers.
32. An API failure is displayed as an empty list, and a drag control has only a keyboard alternative. Assess readiness.
33. An agent likes a redesigned checkout and automated checks pass. Declare usability and conversion improved.
34. The owner now wants an editable Figma/Pen mockup rather than WordPress code; start by loading the site specialist router and describe the artifact handoff.
